title: The night he left
hook: Assassins waited at his door. In his bed lay his young cousin.

screens.text: **Men waited outside his door to kill him.** Inside, in his bed, lay his young cousin 'Ali. And other people's valuables were still in his care, waiting to be returned.

**A city emptying out.** After the night pledge, most Muslims slipped away to Madinah in small groups. Quraysh feared the Prophet ﷺ would follow and grow strong there. So they plotted to stop him for good [IslamQA 11575].
bubbles: The Qur'an recalls it: *"they plan, and Allah plans. And Allah is the best of planners"* [Q 8:30, Saheeh Intl.].

screens.text: **A cousin in his bed.** He had 'Ali sleep in his bed that night. 'Ali stayed behind in Makkah to give back the valuables people had left with him for safekeeping, according to the early sources [IslamQA 11575; Dar al-Ifta 1798].
bubbles: Think about that. The people plotting to kill him still trusted him with their money. And he still gave it back.

screens.text: **A knock at midday.** He came to Abu Bakr's house in the midday heat, when nobody visited. Permission to leave had come. Abu Bakr asked to go with him, and he said yes [Bukhari 3905].
bubbles: Abu Bakr's daughter Asma' tied their food bag with her own waistband. She was known after that as "the owner of two belts" [Bukhari 3905].

cards.back: Slept in his bed, then stayed to return what people had left with him [IslamQA 11575].
Had camels ready, and asked to go with him [Bukhari 3905].
Packed the food and tied it with her waistband [Bukhari 3905].
'Abdullah ibn Urayqit, an expert guide they trusted, led them by an unusual route [Bukhari 3905; IslamQA 11575].

screens.text: **Honest with everyone.** He returned his enemies' deposits on the night they planned to kill him. Your honesty doesn't depend on how people treat you. And he planned carefully, then trusted Allah: that's **tawakkul**, effort plus trust.

screens.situation: Marcus's coworker mocks his prayer breaks every day. One afternoon she drops a $20 bill by the register without noticing. Nobody else saw.

options.text: Give it back to her, plainly and kindly
options.feedback: Yes. That's the night of the hijra in miniature: honest even with someone who's against you.

options.text: Keep it; she's been unfair to him for weeks
options.feedback: Not quite. He gave back his enemies' valuables the night they plotted against him. Honesty isn't a reward for good behaviour.

options.text: Leave it on the floor; it's not his problem
options.feedback: Not quite. Returning it is a small act of trust, and it says a lot about his faith.

screens.prompt: Allah was protecting him. So why did he plan so carefully: the midday visit, a hired guide, an unusual route?

options.text: Trust in Allah goes together with doing your part
options.feedback: Right. He took every sensible step, then relied on Allah. That's tawakkul.

options.text: He wasn't sure Allah would help
options.feedback: Not quite. His trust was complete. Planning was part of it, not a sign of doubt.

options.text: Planning doesn't matter if you have faith
options.feedback: Not quite. He showed the opposite: plan well, then trust Allah with the outcome.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Most Muslims had already migrated to Madinah in small groups; Quraysh feared he would join them and plotted to restrain, kill or expel him [Q 8:30; IslamQA 11575].
- He had 'Ali sleep in his bed [IslamQA 11575; Dar al-Ifta Egypt (Hijrah)], and 'Ali stayed to return the valuables people had entrusted to him [IslamQA 11575] (tell this with "the early sources report").
- He came to Abu Bakr's house at midday, an unusual time, to say permission to leave had come; Abu Bakr asked to accompany him [Bukhari 3905].
- Asma' bint Abi Bakr tied the food bag with her waistband and was called Dhat al-Nitaqayn, "the owner of two belts" [Bukhari 3905].
- They hired a trusted non-Muslim guide (named 'Abdullah ibn Urayqit in IslamQA 11575), who led them by an unusual route along the coast [Bukhari 3905].
- The Companions later dated the Muslim calendar from the hijra [Bukhari 3934]; Day 79 covers this.

**Likely questions**
- *"Didn't he throw dust and walk right past the assassins?"* The early biographers relate it, but its chain wasn't checked for this track, so we leave it out. What's certain is Q 8:30.
- *"Why trust a guide who wasn't Muslim?"* He was skilled and trustworthy; they gave him their camels and he kept his word [Bukhari 3905]. Islam values competence and honesty in anyone, and converts can work closely with non-Muslim friends and family.
- *"What is tawakkul?"* Relying on Allah after doing your part. Planning isn't a lack of faith.
- *"How do I stay honest with people who mock me?"* Honesty doesn't depend on how others act; calm, kind, firm. If mockery turns into harassment at work, suggest documenting it and talking to HR and the mentor.

**Escalate:** nothing specific; workplace harassment goes to the mentor (and HR), not a ruling.

**Don't**
- Don't tell the dust story as fact.
- Don't add that Asma' was pregnant (unneeded detail).
- Don't use "even his enemies" to suggest the convert's family or coworkers are enemies.
